task: Task 1 — slugify: drop punctuation and collapse separator runs
interfaces: slugify(title) keeps its name, its single positional parameter, and returns a str
src/slugify.py stays importable as `from slugify import slugify` with src/ on PYTHONPATH; do not turn src/ into a package and do not add __init__.py

acceptance.expect: all pass, including a case asserting slugify('Hello,  World!') == 'hello-world'

constraints: Reachability: src/slugify.py defines one pure function with no imports, and nothing else in this repository imports it (README.md is prose only). The unittest suite over tests/ is therefore the full reachable set; there is no wider baseline to run.
pytest is NOT installed in this environment. Use unittest from the standard library only. A report claiming a pytest run is false evidence.
The tests directory does not exist yet; create tests/test_slugify.py. Create nothing outside write_paths.
TDD is required: write the failing test first and record the observed RED counts, then implement and record the observed GREEN counts. Both phases must be real observed output, not predicted.
Do not run git add, git commit, or any other Git mutation. Root commits.

The slug rule, which is settled and not yours to redesign: lowercase the input; treat every character that is not an ASCII letter or digit as a separator; collapse each run of one or more separators into a single hyphen; strip leading and trailing hyphens.
Cover at least these cases in tests: 'Hello,  World!' -> 'hello-world'; 'Top 10!' -> 'top-10'; '  padded  ' -> 'padded'; 'a - b' -> 'a-b'; '!!!' -> ''; '' -> ''.
expected_result: slugify('Hello,  World!') returns 'hello-world'. Punctuation is removed rather than retained, and any run of spaces or punctuation becomes exactly one hyphen, with no leading or trailing hyphen in the result.
